newsitem.title: USA: NFL american football-PANTHERS' BIAKABUTUKA OUT FOR THE YEAR.
newsitem.headline: NFL american football-PANTHERS' BIAKABUTUKA OUT FOR THE YEAR.

text.p: The Carolina Panthers' Zairean-born rookie running back Tim Biakabutuka will miss the rest of the 1996 NFL season after tests revealed a torn anterior cruciate ligament in his left knee Monday.
Biakabutuka suffered the injury in the first half of Carolina's 24-14 loss at Jacksonville Sunday and did not return. He had just four carries for 17 yards.

Biakabutuka will undergo surgery in a week to 10 days after swelling in the knee subsides, Dr Donald D'Alessandro, the team's orthopedic surgeon, announced. He added that the running back will require an eight-month rehabilitation period, making him ready for the 1997 season training camp.
"It is a commonly performed football surgery and should result in a full recovery for the future," D'Alessandro said.

Biakabutuka, Carolina's first-round pick and the eighth overall selection in the 1996 draft, led the Panthers with 229 rushing yards in four games. He missed most of the preseason due to a contract dispute, but still averaged 22 carries in Carolina's first three games.
Biakabutuka, who was born in Zaire and grew up in Montreal, was the second running back drafted after Lawrence Phillips.

The former Michigan star will be replaced on the roster by free agent running back Leroy Hoard. Hoard, another Michigan product, was released by Baltimore last week after carrying 15 times for 61 yards in the 1996 season.

The Panthers also announced that defensive lineman Mike Fox and guard Frank Garcia will miss three-to-four weeks with injuries. Fox suffered a strained arch in his left foot, while Garcia fractured a bone in his left foot.
